subject: Partner marketplace private offer — pricing walk-through & unit-econ alignment
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@amazon.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@signalbyte.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Partner marketplace private offer — pricing walk-through & unit-econ alignment

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and a few asks so we can move the private-offer draft forward. High level we heard SignalByte's target is to keep effective spend near $700–$900 per 1M tokens (monthly commitment window), with an expected starting volume band of ~200M–400M tokens/month and a scale target of up to ~1B tokens if the pilot looks good.

Key open questions for the group:
- Marketplace flow: confirm whether the buyer will be charged the private-offer "list" price (the price visible in the AWS/GCP marketplace) and what the fee split is (percentage taken by marketplace / reseller). We need the math so we can map list price -> Redwood net revenue per 1M tokens.
- Fee assumptions: are there standard marketplace fees we should model (e.g., 12% listing fee + any reseller adjustments) or will this be negotiated per private offer?
- Target unit economics: SignalByte's procurement needs a net Redwood price that results in ≤ $900 effective buyer cost per 1M tokens. We should show sample scenarios at 200M, 400M, and 1B tokens.

As next steps: Sarah — can you share the marketplace private-offer template with the columns for buyer price, AWS fee %, and customer invoice mechanics? Emily — can you confirm the internal budget cadence and whether SignalByte prefers a monthly or annual committed SKU for the pilot? Marissa / Rishi — I'll need a quick proforma showing net to Redwood given a couple of list price points (I'll attach a starter workbook).

Attachments: redwood-private-offer-proforma.xlsx (starter worksheet)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0164

From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@amazon.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner marketplace private offer — pricing walk-through & unit-econ alignment

Hi Jordan / Emily —

Thanks for the summary. Quick notes from the AWS Marketplace side and the attached template.

1) Buyer billing flow and pricing fields: the marketplace private offer shows a Buyer Price (what the customer sees/gets billed) and an Enterprise Product Price (what you register). AWS Marketplace charges a transaction fee that is normally 12% of Buyer Price for SaaS/usage-based offers. That fee is taken before disbursement. The net to Redwood = Buyer Price - AWS fee - any negotiated reseller/partner margin.

2) Private offer flexibility: you can set a Buyer Price per unit (we support usage-based units). For our template I filled example rows for 1M-token units. Columns included: SKU, BuyerPrice_per_1M_tokens, AWS_fee_pct, Net_to_Seller_per_1M, Effective_buyer_cost_per_1M (same as BuyerPrice), and Notes. See attached aws-private-offer-pricing-template.xlsx.

3) Billing cadence: AWS invoices the buyer; payment terms are between buyer and AWS (default net 30 but can vary). Disbursement to the seller usually occurs monthly (subject to AWS settlement cycles).

4) Negotiables: Some enterprise deals include reduced AWS fees via partnership programs or marketplace credits (rare, requires partner approval). If you have a target Net_to_Seller we can work backwards to suggest BuyerPrice levels and flag where additional partner discounts might be required.

Suggested immediate next step: I can populate three BuyerPrice scenarios so you can compare net to Redwood at 200M / 400M / 1B token volumes. If that sounds good, I'll send the populated sheet today.

Attachment: aws-private-offer-pricing-template.xlsx

Cheers,
Sarah Miller
AWS Marketplace Sales
sarah.miller@amazon.com

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@signalbyte.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner marketplace private offer — pricing walk-through & unit-econ alignment

Jordan / Sarah — thanks for the clarity. A few datapoints from SignalByte procurement:
- Pilot budget window: up to $250k/month for the first 3 months, with a view to scale to $500k+/month if model matches expectations.
- Target: want effective buyer cost <= $900 per 1M tokens at pilot volumes (200M–300M/m). If the price is below $800 /1M we can consider an accelerated kickoff with a 6-month committed SKU.
- Procurement asks: show net-to-seller and buyer price scenarios with clear notes on who invoices (AWS) and how refunds/credits are handled (we need a 90-day data/usage reconciliation clause).

If you can get me two example BuyerPrice points (one aggressive at ~$850/1M, one conservative at ~$1,050/1M) with the AWS fee line shown, we can do an internal run and confirm which band fits the $250k/mo cap.

Regards,
Emily Chen
Head of Procurement, SignalByte
emily.chen@signalbyte.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@signalbyte.com>, Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner marketplace private offer — pricing walk-through & unit-econ alignment

Appreciate the fast turnaround, team — I ran quick math in the attached proforma and here are two scenario snapshots (net numbers rounded):

Scenario A (aggressive buyer price):
- BuyerPrice_per_1M = $850
- AWS fee (12%) = $102 -> Net to Redwood ≈ $748/1M
- Effective buyer cost = $850 -> fits Emily's <= $900 target; at 250M tokens/month buyer spend ≈ $212.5k/month. Redwood net revenue ≈ $187k/month.

Scenario B (conservative buyer price):
- BuyerPrice_per_1M = $1,050
- AWS fee (12%) = $126 -> Net to Redwood ≈ $924/1M
- Effective buyer cost = $1,050 -> above Emily's pilot cap but gives Redwood more headroom for discounts / margin. At 250M tokens/month buyer spend ≈ $262.5k/month.

Notes / implications:
- If the AWS fee can be reduced even 2–3 percentage points via partner credits that shifts Net to Redwood materially (e.g., at $850/1M a 9% fee -> net ≈ $773). Sarah — please flag if there are partner programs that could apply here.
- We should align on whether SignalByte prefers an annual committed SKU (lower unit price) vs monthly ramp (more flexibility). Emily, you hinted that <$800/1M unlocks a 6-month commit — we should quantify that band and add to the draft PO.
- I'll prepare a private-offer draft PDF for SignalByte to review (attaching PO-draft-Redwood-SignalByte.pdf). Marissa / Rishi: can you spin up a final proforma row set reflecting these two BuyerPrice points plus a third break-even price where Redwood net = $700/1M?

Attached: redwood-private-offer-proforma.xlsx, PO-draft-Redwood-SignalByte.pdf

On the call next week we should finalize: BuyerPrice target, whether commit is monthly vs annual, settlement cadence, and any marketplace fee reduction paths. I'll propose a 30-minute follow-up Tuesday (Jun 23).

Best,
Jordan
